event_data.context:
Implementation notes

Architecture and trust boundary
- Use microvm.nix to provide a NixOS MicroVM with the repository mounted read/write at /work and used as the initial working directory.
- The writable repository, including flake.nix, must never be evaluated on the host while creating or launching the security boundary. Do not implement the launch path as nix run .#codex-vm, host-side nix develop, nix print-dev-env, direnv evaluation, or any equivalent project-controlled host evaluation.
- Put the trusted runner outside the writable project domain, such as a separately pinned trusted flake, a NixOS or Home Manager package, or a separately maintained launcher. Repository-local configuration may be parsed only as data through a small declarative schema with strict validation; it must not execute shell or Nix code on the host.
- Clearly separate and document trusted host infrastructure from agent-writable project configuration.

Guest filesystem and persistence
- Share only explicitly authorized paths. Mount this repository read/write at /work.
- Persist Codex configuration, state, and authentication in a dedicated per-project host directory mounted as /home/agent/.codex or, if required, as a dedicated /home/agent. Never mount the developer’s real home directory.
- Prefer a VM-owned /nix/store. Do not share the host store without first documenting and justifying the security/performance tradeoff.
- Keep the rest of the guest root filesystem ephemeral where practical.
- Do not expose the host home directory, SSH agent, Docker or Podman sockets, host /tmp, host process namespaces, arbitrary host devices, or implicit host credentials.
- If extra shares are supported, require explicit paths, explicit read-only/read-write mode, canonical path validation, and a non-executable project configuration format.

Networking
- Provide outbound Internet access for OpenAI, GitHub, Nix substituters, and package registries.
- Minimize access from the guest to host services. Research the host-reachability properties of QEMU user networking and implement a more isolated practical option when available; otherwise document the precise remaining limitation and mitigation.

Developer experience
- Provide Git, Nix, certificates, common shell tools, and what is needed to bootstrap this repository.
- Evaluate the repository flake and enter its existing development shell only inside the guest so dependencies are not duplicated unnecessarily.
- Install a current Codex CLI from an appropriately pinned Nix source/package. Configure Codex for broad guest filesystem and process access because the MicroVM is the sandbox.
- Support first-time device authentication and make codex-vm drop directly into Codex in /work when practical.
- Use project-specific persistent state with a deterministic, collision-resistant location and document how it is derived and cleaned up.

Research and prior art
- Inspect the repository’s existing Nix and host-oriented structure first.
- Use current upstream documentation for microvm.nix, NixOS MicroVM QEMU settings, Codex CLI installation and authentication/state paths, and networking isolation.
- Evaluate systemstart/claude-microvm as prior art, especially Codex support, but independently address host-side project evaluation, host Nix store sharing, network isolation, and per-project state.

Project and host deliverables
- Implement the project-side portion in this repository.
- Provide a clearly separated, movable example for any trusted launcher or configuration that correctly belongs in NixOS/Home Manager rather than the writable repository.
- Document the architecture; exact install/setup and launch commands; first authentication; state location; adding an explicit share; remaining security limitations, especially networking; and the trust classification of every relevant file.
- Test evaluation/build/launch behavior as far as the current environment permits and fix obvious Nix errors before completion.
event_data.summary: Enable repository development with Codex inside a project-specific virtual machine that acts as the primary boundary protecting the host. A trusted launcher, maintained outside the agent-writable repository, should start the environment with one simple command. The repository remains writable inside the environment, Codex state persists per project, and no ordinary host files or credentials are exposed. This matters because Codex must be able to build, test, and modify the project without gaining the same access as a process running directly on the developer’s machine.
event_data.title: Isolate Codex development from the host machine
